description: ORDER BY is compiled from a schema-declared key, never from input. The clause is the one place a dialect changes more than spelling: MySQL has no NULLS LAST and sorts on an IS NULL expression first instead. An unknown key is a diagnostic and no clause.

cases.name: ascending, nulls last
cases.orderBy: ORDER BY doc.name ASC NULLS LAST

cases.name: descending
cases.orderBy: ORDER BY doc.name DESC NULLS LAST

cases.name: the key selects a host-supplied expression, not a column name
cases.orderBy: ORDER BY doc.state ASC NULLS LAST

cases.name: duckdb spells it the same way
cases.orderBy: ORDER BY doc.name DESC NULLS LAST

cases.name: sqlite spells it the same way
cases.orderBy: ORDER BY doc.name ASC NULLS LAST

cases.name: mysql has no NULLS LAST and sorts on IS NULL first
cases.orderBy: ORDER BY doc.name IS NULL, doc.name ASC

cases.name: mysql, descending
cases.orderBy: ORDER BY doc.name IS NULL, doc.name DESC

cases.name: an unknown key is a diagnostic and no clause
an empty key is not an error; the host simply is not sorting
